title: Days Charged When a Bundled Umbrella or Floater Ends — RentGuard Renters Policy
content:
Stop courtesy period on the RentGuard Renters Policy: the days charged for the multi-policy discount stop depend on how the ending qualifying policy — the Larkspur Personal Umbrella Policy or Larkspur Valuables Floater whose end stopped the discount — came to end, as its own record shows it (status reason, bound date, closed date).

**Clause.** When the ending qualifying policy was cancelled at its named insured's request and had been held for 12 whole months or more from its bound date to its closed date, the days charged for the stop are the calendar days from its closed date to the renters expiration date less 30; when the ending qualifying policy was cancelled for nonpayment, the days charged for the stop are the calendar days of the whole renters term from its effective date, because a qualifying policy left unpaid never earned the discount; in every other case the days charged for the stop run from the closed date.

### Decision table

| How the umbrella or floater ended | Whole months held, bound date to closed date | Days charged for the stop |
|---|---|---|
| Cancelled at its named insured's request | 12 or more | Calendar days from its closed date to the renters expiration date, less 30 |
| Cancelled at its named insured's request | 11 or fewer | Calendar days from its closed date to the renters expiration date |
| Cancelled for nonpayment | any | Calendar days of the whole renters term, from the renters effective date to the renters expiration date |
| Any other ending, such as expiry at the end of its term | any | Calendar days from its closed date to the renters expiration date |

### Boundary cases (hypothetical)

- A floater bound on 10 March of one year and cancelled at the insured's request on 10 March of the next year has been held 12 whole months: the 30-day courtesy is taken off. Cancelled on 9 March instead, it has been held 11 whole months and the days run in full from the closed date.
- Hypothetical figures: 200 calendar days from the closed date to the renters expiration date become 170 days charged under the courtesy period.
- An umbrella cancelled for nonpayment after any length of holding makes the whole renters term the days charged, whatever its closed date.
